activities.caption: pair each system with what touch does to it
activities.name: mtSystemMatch

config.prompt: Touch engages a working set of systems — pair each with its effect:

pairs.right: slow, broad, rhythmic pressure shifts the autonomic balance toward the parasympathetic "rest and digest" state
compressing and releasing tissue assists venous return — which is why classical strokes run centripetally, toward the heart
a one-way vessel network with no pump of its own — light, rhythmic strokes assist the drainage
the contact surface and barrier, inspected before every session; the tissue skin rolling acts on
cortisol drops while serotonin and oxytocin rise — "relaxation" becomes a measurable event

config.why: The eleven-system filing is made by human minds, not the flesh — but it tells a therapist exactly where each effect of touch lives.

activities.anchor: It sounds right because muscles genuinely feel different afterwards
activities.caption: find the line the physiology refutes
activities.name: mtToxinsSpot

config.prompt: One line of this massage explanation is wrong — click it:
lines: Touch modulates nervous-system state — that is the physiological basis of the calm clients report.
Massage assists fluid movement in veins and lymphatics.
Deep kneading flushes accumulated toxins out of the muscle.
Touch influences tone and connective tissue — real, measurable effects.
A therapist who can say exactly what touch does is more convincing than one who promises what it does not.
config.correction: Nothing is flushed out and nothing is physically reshaped the way the popular picture suggests — the honest effects are modulation, fluid movement and tone change.
config.why: Precision here is part of professionalism.

activities.anchor: Muscles also work as a team
activities.caption: walk the team plan for an overworked muscle
activities.name: mtTeamBranch

config.root: Much of what clients feel as tension is one muscle overworking while its antagonist has stopped doing its share.

start.text: The upper trapezius is overworked; its opposite number has gone quiet. The treatment plan?

choices.label: Release the overworked AND re-educate the underworked

half.text: That quiets the loud member and leaves the imbalance — treatment plans talk about releasing the overworked AND re-educating the underworked.

both.text: Agonist is the prime mover, antagonist opposes and brakes, synergists assist and steady — the plan restores the team, not just the sore spot.

roles.text: In a biceps curl, which role does the triceps play as the elbow bends?

choices.label: The antagonist — opposing and braking the movement

right.text: Antagonist: it opposes the prime mover and brakes the movement — while synergists assist and steady it.

wrong.text: Synergists assist and steady the movement — the opposing, braking role belongs to the antagonist.

config.why: Rope logic: where a muscle is anchored and where it pulls decides what moves.

config.q: Connective tissue — fascia, tendons, ligaments — is stiff when cold or pulled fast, pliable when warm and stretched slowly. The working consequence:
choices: press harder to defeat the stiffness quickly
warm the tissue and work slowly — a sustained hold changes tissue feel in ways a quick press cannot
ice the area first to stiffen it further
config.why: Viscoelastic behaviour is why a therapist warms tissue before working deeper — and why a sustained hold does what a quick press cannot.

activities.anchor: The muscle's own physiology closes the loop
activities.caption: file each tone-change by its mechanism
activities.name: mtToneBuckets

config.prompt: "Releasing" a muscle has two honest mechanisms — file each move:

items.label: slow pressure and sustained holds that persuade the nervous system
the nervous system keeping a resting muscle on standby
warmth and fluid exchange in the tissue itself
fascial shear through the collagen web
the baseline stiffness of the tissue itself

config.why: Tone is partly neural and partly structural — techniques differ, but both paths run through the same anatomy.

activities.anchor: its vocabulary is what makes assessment honest
activities.caption: rebuild the movement vocabulary by plane
activities.name: mtPlanesOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the vocabulary from anatomical position, plane by plane:
items: Sagittal plane — the side view: flexion and extension, bending and straightening
Frontal plane — the front view: abduction and adduction, away from and toward the midline
Transverse plane — the top view: rotation around a segment's long axis
Then the specials: pronation/supination of the forearm, inversion/eversion of the foot, elevation/depression of the scapula
config.why: Movement is described from anatomical position — standing, facing forward, palms forward, the universal reference stance.

activities.anchor: one division the practitioner uses constantly
activities.caption: true or false — fibre types
activities.name: mtFibreJudge

statements.s: Slow-twitch (Type I) fibres dominate the deep back, neck and calf muscles that complain in desk workers.
statements.why: Endurance specialists — dense with mitochondria, fatigue-resistant, doing the postural work.
They are power specialists — quick to contract and quick to fatigue, dominating burst muscles like the hamstrings.

statements.s: The marathon runner's hamstring and the office worker's trapezius need different sessions even when both report "tightness".
statements.why: Postural muscles accumulate low-grade chronic tension; power muscles take acute strain from burst effort.

statements.s: The honest assessment question is "tight or relaxed?".
statements.why: It is "what is this muscle being asked to do all day?" — the answer tells you whether you are treating endurance fatigue or acute strain.

activities.anchor: A professional session runs a shape every school teaches
activities.caption: rebuild the session arc
activities.name: mtSessionOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the session arc from door to re-test:
items: Intake — health history and today's goal, translated into movement language and contraindication screening
Draping and positioning — dignity first, and a well-supported body lets its muscles switch off
Warm-up strokes that assess while they soothe — temperature, tone and guarding all read through light effleurage
The specific work — deeper pressure along fibre direction, sustained holds where the nervous system releases tone
Re-assessment — the same movement retested, the same words recorded
config.why: Every hands-on session is the systems map, the muscle grammar and the movement vocabulary — applied through controlled pressure.
